issues.description: The 'from' detection is correct but complects parser-tree shape with relative-color semantics via an offset trick.
issues.detail: The fix is small and works, but the function now encodes 'relative color' as an arithmetic offset into a positional args array. The value being computed is 'which arg is the hue channel'; expressing that as a +2 shift hides the meaning. A small helper like getChannels(node) returning the post-'from' word/function nodes would make the data flow explicit.

issues.description: args[0]?.value.toLowerCase() assumes a shape that isn't asserted; the value being inspected is implicit.
issues.detail: args is filtered to word|function, but only word nodes carry a meaningful string 'from'. A function node's .value is the function name, which could coincidentally be 'from' in pathological input. Checking args[0]?.type === 'word' alongside the value comparison would make the fact being tested explicit and immutable.

issues.description: Nested relative-color cases (oklch(from hsl(...) l c h)) are accepted but the inner function's hue is not re-checked here.
issues.detail: The accept test 'oklch(from hsl(270deg 60% 50%) l c h)' passes because outer channels are non-numeric, but findHue only inspects the top node. Whether the inner hsl() hue gets walked is a separate concern handled elsewhere; worth a one-line comment noting recursion is the caller's job, so the time/scope of this function is explicit.

review.summary: The change is small, localized, and correctly handles the relative-color syntax that the rule was missing. My concern is not correctness but how the fact 'channels begin after from <origin>' is expressed: as a numeric offset added to array indices, which complects the parse-tree shape with the color-syntax semantics. A tiny helper that returns the channel nodes as data would make the value, the identity (which arg is the hue), and the time (when 'from' shifts the window) explicit. SIMPLE enough to ship; EASY-NOT-SIMPLE in how the offset is encoded. No P0 or P1 blockers.
